Maintain saved Outlook data and its official next-release schedule

Source: R/outlook-maintenance.R
maintain_boj_outlook.Rd

A scheduler can invoke this hourly. A not-due call reads local state only. Due daily revision checks use the full incremental updater. Around an overdue release, cheap archive/HEAD probes trigger a forced update only after links, dates or validators change. Bank's View and next-business-day full text remain separate pending stages. Every update recomputes the next due time from fresh official calendar evidence. No OS job or background worker is installed.

Usage

maintain_boj_outlook(
  data_dir = boj_outlook_data_dir(),
  force = FALSE,
  calendar_max_age = 86400,
  revision_interval = 86400,
  probe_interval = 3600,
  timeout = 30,
  retries = 2L,
  deadline = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data_dir

Persistent directory shared with ordinary saved reads.

force

Ignore maintenance timing and run a full source/calendar check.

calendar_max_age, revision_interval

Seconds between calendar refreshes and complete historical source revision checks (defaults one day).

probe_interval

Minimum seconds between release-window metadata probes.

timeout, retries, deadline

Bounded request/deadline settings.

...

Additional arguments for update_boj_outlook(), such as a Poppler path. Maintenance never enables coverage-loss opt-in automatically.

Value

A list with status, scalar ISO8601 UTC next_due_at, release/date/ edition, separate full-text pending state, freshness and errors. Operational failures return failed and a persisted bounded retry schedule, preserving last-good numeric data and calendar. Busy writers return busy for retry.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# A scheduler and ordinary readers should share one persistent directory.
maintain_boj_outlook(data_dir = boj_outlook_data_dir(),
                     deadline = Sys.time() + 1800)
} # }
